_doc: SITE CONFIG (W4, 2026-08-02). The one place the owner's identity is written down.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The X handle was hard-coded in build/prerender.js:494 (the Organization
JSON-LD sameAs, which reaches every prerendered page) and a personal username was sitting in the
sign-in modal's placeholder as `e.g. hyrox_felix` -- measured hydrated at 390x844 by opening the
modal on /. Three of the four X-loop surfaces added in this wave print the handle, so without a
config there would have been seven hard-coded copies of one string across three files.
VOICE. `x.handle` is a PERSONAL account belonging to ONE INDIVIDUAL. There is no company, no
editorial board and no clinical service. Every string generated from this file must read as one
person speaking. assertSingleVoice() and assertNoCredentialClaims() in build/parse.js already
fail the build on the opposite, and assertHandleFromConfig() fails it if the handle is typed
into a renderer again.
`handle` is stored WITHOUT the leading @ and must match X's own rule: 1-15 characters,
letters/digits/underscore only. parse.js validates it and refuses to build otherwise, because
an invalid handle silently produces a share link to a profile that does not exist.
NOT A CREDENTIAL. Nothing here asserts that the account holder is a clinician, is qualified, or
has reviewed anything. It is a name and three links.
THE NINE CHIPS ON /interest, and the write schema for interest_signups.topic (2026-08-08).
ONE definition, read twice: build/prerender.js renders the radio group from it, and server.js
validates POST /api/interest against it (loaded at boot out of site/data.js, the same way the
compound aliases and the /solve index are). Two hand-kept copies of an allowlist drift; a
set-membership test against one array cannot. The labels are the owner's own, verbatim from
his wireframe, in his order.
`id` IS STORED IN THE DATABASE and is matched exactly by the server. Changing a label is safe.
Changing an id orphans every row already stored under the old one, so do not.
The chip with id `other` is not optional: it is the one that reveals the free-text field, and
topic_other is only ever stored when it is the chosen answer. parse.js refuses to build
without it.
